public_rationale: The 2024 navigation experiments recovered incoherent maps despite strong task performance [e1]. A separate 2024 study found that a chess-trained language model learned board representations without supplied chess rules, and interventions changed its behavior [e2]. The June 3, 2025 spatial study reported causally used representations in Llama but did not test movement or temporal dynamics [e3]. The evidence shows both coherence failures and learned representations beyond Othello, without settling whether the chess result meets the intended scope, completeness and reliability standard [e1, e2, e3].
limitations: Failures in the tested navigation systems do not establish categorical non-emergence across LLMs [e1].
The chess study leaves complete state tracking, robustness and applicability to general-purpose LLMs unsettled [e2].
The spatial study does not address temporal dynamics, movement or object permanence [e3].

public_payload.normalized_proposition: Proper world models do not emerge on their own in LLMs.

statement.excerpt: One hopes that proper world models will simply “emerge” — but they don’t.
statement.document_title: Generative AI’s crippling and widespread failure to induce robust models of the world

from_speaker: reliably maintains and uses a full model
our_interpretation: The plain reading concerns coherent internal representations that track a domain and reliably guide predictions as its state changes. Merely recalling facts or decoding a feature is insufficient; perfect performance is not required.
Emergence means that the representation develops through training without an explicitly programmed world model. Training a model on domain-specific text does not automatically disqualify it.
The observation concerns what had emerged by publication. Earlier demonstrations remain relevant; there is no June-only restriction or source-specified starting date.
The acknowledged Othello result alone cannot refute the claim. Specialized models beyond Othello are relevant, but their applicability to general-purpose LLMs must be stated.
criteria.support_condition: Representative studies of relevant models find that apparently learned representations fail to remain coherent, update correctly, or guide predictions reliably across the tested domains. Limited failures alone cannot establish a categorical absence.
criteria.contradiction_condition: A reproducible demonstration beyond the acknowledged Othello example shows a learned internal representation that coherently tracks changing states and reliably guides predictions, without an explicitly engineered world model.

evidence.explanation: The navigation experiments found incoherent reconstructed maps despite strong task performance. This supports the concern about coherence in the tested systems, without establishing that all LLMs lack proper world models.

evidence.locator: Section 4.2, Board State Interventions; Sections 2.2 and 3.1
evidence.explanation: A chess-trained GPT developed board representations without supplied chess rules, and activation interventions changed its behavior. This is substantial counterevidence to non-emergence beyond Othello, but leaves the intended scope and completeness standard unsettled.

The study reports spatial representations and causal steering in Llama, but explicitly excludes movement and other components of a full world model. Its positive result cannot by itself settle Marcus's stronger dynamic-model claim.

public_payload.what_would_resolve: Clarify the intended model scope and completeness standard, then provide reproducible tests of models existing by June 28, 2025 showing whether learned representations coherently update and causally guide reliable predictions in unfamiliar situations. A qualifying demonstration beyond Othello would contradict the claim; representative failures would support it.
